Feedback Senate: It's pretty clear from the brief discussion of the strategic plan today and the exchange with the President that faculty are not feeling awesome in general or like UW particularly values them. I realize that the President is right: these are tough times for higher ed. But I believe the faculty are right also. This place needs to get the vibes right. Former President Cauce used to speak of the abuse of, or the UW riding for far too long on, the "Rainier factor" -- that this place is lovely for many people and therefore we are willing to settle for less of many things. That remains true. UW at the administrative level is not really trying to do more than keep the lights on, keep the legislature from cutting more, and keep the donors happy. All good goals, surely. But I've been here for 15 years and it feels very much like UW's view is "enjoy it or leave it, we don't really need you and could replace you with someone else who wants to be here instead." True as that may be -- this is a great region to be for all kinds of reasons and people want to come here -- I'd like to see UW maybe, you know, do a little better than that. You have the people you have. We want to be here and would like to feel like the place wants us here. We are generally pretty good and often public spirited, even if replaceable. And it would be nice to actually indicate an effort to lift faculty up rather than negotiate them to the minimum. The UW cannot control the whims of the legislature, the Congress, or housing supply or living costs in the region. But it has total control of its institutional mindset, its message, and its attitude toward faculty. If UW can't pay people more because the state caps tuition and cuts the budget and changes the fund split, if UW is scrapping to preserve federal funding and the traditional overhead rate, if UW cannot make more children go to college or change the demographic cliff, sure, it is fair to tell everyone that. It feels, though, like the overall UW approach is: well, we've said that and communicated the information accurately and with a tone of dismay; make handwashing motion; done and dusted. Aren't those the circumstances in which it makes more sense to give people something else they crave and that is within an organization's sole control? A sense of shared mission, or a sense of belonging, a sense of value or public contribution? A story to belong to or be part of? None of this is easy. But, as someone who understands the real constraints and challenges the UW is challenging, I nonetheless share the sense that -- to the extent there is a UW-wide or top-level vibe -- this is not a place that particularly cares whether particular faculty stay or go, or that we are valued beyond being workers for a wage. There's a real lack of inspiration. Is this a Senate problem? Not really, other than it feels more and more likely that calls (ultimately not ones I'd support, probably) for unionization will rise the more it feels like we are being undervalued and underpaid, and then the mode of the Senate ceases to have any use.
